agents.label: Design QA
agents.summary: The Corporate Counsel & Compliance Exchange USA microsite communicates the essential event information and has a recognisable brand identity, but falls short of professional standards across several axes. The most pressing issues are inconsistent button colours that deviate from brand config, a fragmented mobile experience with stacking and contrast problems, and a lack of typographic discipline (Raleway is used instead of the specified Archivo/Inter pair). With targeted fixes the page could reach a publishable standard, but as-is it reads as marketer-built rather than designer-built.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Stats row (desktop, between hero and speakers section)
findings.issue: The four stat blocks (75, 22, 194, 27) appear to use unequal column widths, with the fourth stat visually narrower and its label wrapping differently to the others, breaking the grid rhythm.
findings.recommendation: Constrain all four stat items to equal Bootstrap col-3 (or CSS grid fr) columns with a shared max-width so numbers, labels, and supporting text align on the same baseline.
findings.fix_prompt: In the stats row section, set all four stat columns to `col-3` in Bootstrap (or `grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr)` in CSS) and add `text-align: center` and equal horizontal padding (e.g. `px-3`) to each cell so all four items share identical widths and internal spacing.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Sponsorship Opportunities section, desktop
findings.issue: The 'Sponsorship Opportunities' text block and the adjacent image sit at different vertical baselines with visible unequal left/right padding, making the two-column layout look misaligned rather than intentional.
findings.recommendation: Use a Bootstrap row with align-items-center on the parent and equal col-md-6 children, ensuring both columns share the same vertical midpoint.
findings.fix_prompt: Wrap the sponsorship image and copy in `<div class='row align-items-center'>` with each child as `<div class='col-md-6 px-4'>`. Remove any inline margin or padding overrides on the individual columns so Bootstrap's gutter handles spacing uniformly.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Past Leaders logo cloud, desktop
findings.issue: Sponsor/past-leader logos wrap onto multiple rows but rows are not evenly filled — the final row has only 3 logos left-aligned against 6 on earlier rows, creating an orphaned cluster.
findings.recommendation: Use CSS flexbox with justify-content: center on the logo container so partial final rows are centred rather than left-hanging.
findings.fix_prompt: On the past-leaders logo container element, add `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 24px;` and remove any fixed-column Bootstrap classes from individual logo wrappers so the last row centres automatically.

findings.issue: The rendered page loads 'Raleway' as both primary and secondary font (confirmed in CSS :root variables). The brand config mandates Archivo for headings and Inter for body. No Archivo or Inter import is present in the dynamic styles block.
findings.recommendation: Add Google Fonts imports for Archivo and Inter, then update --primary-font to 'Archivo' and --secondary-font to 'Inter' in the :root CSS block.
findings.fix_prompt: At the top of the dynamic <style> block, replace the existing @import for Raleway with: `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo:wght@400;600;700;800&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap');` Then in :root set `--primary-font: 'Archivo', sans-serif;` and `--secondary-font: 'Inter', sans-serif;`.

findings.location: Typography · Body copy throughout page (desktop and mobile)
findings.issue: Multiple body text paragraphs (e.g. the event description below the hero, the testimonial quote, the sponsorship copy) render at what appears to be 13–14 px in a full-width container with no max-width constraint, producing line lengths well over 100 characters on desktop — far outside the 45–90 character target.
findings.recommendation: Constrain all body-text columns to max-width: 720px (or equivalent ~75 ch) and centre within their container.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a CSS rule: `.body-text-column, .event-description, .testimonial-copy, .sponsorship-copy { max-width: 720px; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; }` Adjust the selector list to match the actual class names used for prose text blocks across the page.

findings.location: Typography · Section headings across page (e.g. '2026 Expert Speakers', 'Key Themes for 2026 Include:', 'Past Leaders on the Board')
findings.issue: Heading sizes appear inconsistent — some section titles render noticeably larger than others at the same semantic H2 level, suggesting inline font-size overrides rather than a consistent type scale.
findings.recommendation: Audit all H2/H3 elements and remove inline font-size overrides; instead rely on the CSS type scale definitions (32px for H2, 24px for H3) from the brand config scale.
findings.fix_prompt: In the dynamic stylesheet, add: `h2 { font-size: 32px !important; line-height: 1.2; } h3 { font-size: 24px !important; line-height: 1.3; }` and remove any conflicting inline `style='font-size:...'` attributes from heading elements in the HTML.

findings.location: Typography · Hero subtitle ('Checkmate, Chaos – Turning Volatility into Your Next Strategic Advantage'), desktop
findings.issue: The subtitle appears in a yellow/gold colour (#ffd230 link colour) applied as a heading, making it look like a hyperlink rather than a thematic subtitle.
findings.recommendation: Set the hero subtitle to white or the brand accent (#FF5A36) to distinguish it from the event name without mimicking a link state.
findings.fix_prompt: Find the hero subtitle element (likely an H2 or H3 with the class referencing the tagline) and add the inline style or CSS rule: `color: #FFFFFF; text-decoration: none;` to remove the link-colour appearance while maintaining legibility on the dark hero background.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · 'Benefits of Attending / Benefits of Sponsoring' section, desktop
findings.issue: This section appears nearly empty — two tab labels are visible but the content area below them renders with an enormous unexplained void, suggesting hidden or failed-to-load content, leaving a jarring blank band in the page.
findings.recommendation: Audit whether the Benefits content is gated behind a failed API call or CMS entry. If content is not ready, remove the section entirely rather than leaving a visible empty band.
findings.fix_prompt: In the HTML for the Benefits of Attending / Sponsoring section, add `style='display:none'` to the section wrapper element until content is populated, to prevent an empty white band from displaying to visitors.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · Photo Gallery section, desktop
findings.issue: The photo gallery images are cramped with near-zero visible gap between thumbnails while the section heading above has excessive top padding (~80px), creating unbalanced rhythm within the section.
findings.recommendation: Add a consistent 16px gap between gallery images and reduce the section heading top-padding to 48px to match the spacing scale.
findings.fix_prompt: On the photo gallery image container, add `gap: 16px; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap;` and on the gallery section heading, set `padding-top: 48px;` replacing any larger value currently applied.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · CLE Credit badge / Approved for 10.25 CLE Credit Hours row, desktop
findings.issue: The CLE badge and text sit with noticeably less vertical padding than surrounding content bands, making it feel pinched relative to adjacent sections.
findings.recommendation: Add padding: 24px 0 to the CLE row container to match the spacing scale.
findings.fix_prompt: Find the container element wrapping the 'APPROVED FOR 10.25 CLE CREDIT HOURS' row and add `style='padding: 24px 0;'` or a CSS class with `padding-top: 24px; padding-bottom: 24px;` to give it breathing room consistent with neighbouring sections.

findings.issue: Three CTAs appear in the hero bar at near-equal visual weight ('Request Your Invite', 'Download Agenda', 'Sponsorship Opportunities'). All three are similar-sized buttons, so the primary registration CTA does not clearly dominate. The registration CTA should be visually singular.
findings.recommendation: Style 'Request Your Invite' as a filled accent-colour (#FF5A36) button at full weight, and demote 'Download Agenda' and 'Sponsorship Opportunities' to ghost/outline style so hierarchy is unambiguous.
findings.fix_prompt: In the hero button group, give the 'Request Your Invite' button `style='background-color:#FF5A36; color:#FFFFFF; border:none; font-weight:700; padding: 14px 28px;'` and give the other two buttons `style='background-color:transparent; border: 2px solid #FFFFFF; color:#FFFFFF; padding: 12px 24px;'` so the primary CTA is visually dominant.

findings.location: Visual hierarchy · '2026 Sponsorship Opportunities SOLD OUT' banner, desktop
findings.issue: A large high-contrast yellow/orange band announces sponsorship is sold out, which draws significant visual attention mid-page and competes with the registration CTA as a primary call-to-action signal, despite not being actionable for most visitors.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the visual weight of this sold-out announcement — use a smaller inline badge or muted text rather than a full-width accent banner.
findings.fix_prompt: Replace the full-width coloured sold-out banner with an inline `Sponsorship Sold Out` placed next to the section heading, removing the large background-colour block entirely.

findings.issue: The 'VIEW ALL 2026 SPEAKERS' button appears in yellow (#ffd230) against a white background, matching the link colour variable, which gives it secondary-link rather than CTA energy.
findings.recommendation: Use the primary brand colour (#0A2540) as button background or the accent (#FF5A36) so it reads as an actionable button rather than a styled link.
findings.fix_prompt: Find the 'View All 2026 Speakers' button element and set `style='background-color:#0A2540; color:#FFFFFF; border:none; padding:12px 24px; font-weight:600; border-radius:4px;'` replacing the current yellow styling.

findings.location: Consistency · CTAs site-wide (hero, speakers, themes, sponsorship, footer)
findings.issue: Button colours are inconsistent across the page: some buttons are blue (#0081ff, the CSS primary-color), some are yellow (#ffd230), and the hero registration button appears in yet another shade. None of these match the brand-config accent (#FF5A36) reserved for CTAs. At least four distinct button colour treatments are visible.
findings.recommendation: Standardise all primary CTAs to background #FF5A36 with white text, all secondary/ghost CTAs to #0A2540 outline, and remove all yellow (#ffd230) button instances.
findings.fix_prompt: In the dynamic stylesheet :root block, change `--primary-color: #FF5A36;` and `--primary-color-hover: #cc3a20;` and `--secondary-color: #0A2540;`. Then do a find-and-replace in the HTML for any inline `style` attributes with background-color:#0081ff or background-color:#ffd230 on button elements, replacing them with the correct token values.

findings.location: Consistency · Theme cards (Key Themes section) vs Speaker cards, desktop
findings.issue: Theme cards have a yellow top border accent and dark overlay with white text; speaker cards have no border accent and use a different overlay opacity. The card treatment is inconsistent between the two card types, which appear in adjacent sections.
findings.recommendation: Define a single card component spec: consistent corner radius (4px), consistent image overlay style, and consistent heading/body text treatment, then apply uniformly to both speaker and theme cards.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a shared CSS class `.event-card { border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); }` and apply it to both the speaker card elements and the theme card elements. Ensure image overlays on both use `background: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(10,37,64,0.85) 0%, rgba(10,37,64,0) 60%);` for consistency.

findings.issue: Sponsor logos are displayed at varying sizes and with inconsistent vertical alignment — some logos appear roughly twice the height of others in the same row, making the grid look unorganised.
findings.recommendation: Constrain all sponsor logo images to a fixed container height (e.g. 48px) with object-fit: contain and vertical-align: middle so all logos sit at the same optical baseline.
findings.fix_prompt: Add CSS: `.sponsor-logo-grid img { height: 48px; width: auto; max-width: 140px; object-fit: contain; display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; }` — adjust the selector to match the actual class wrapping sponsor logo img elements.

findings.issue: The top navigation 'Request an Invite' button uses a different visual style (appears as a blue pill/rounded button) compared to the hero CTA buttons below, which use a different shape and colour, breaking button consistency from the first visible element.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same button component class and colour (#FF5A36 fill, white text, 4px radius) to the nav CTA as used for the hero primary CTA.
findings.fix_prompt: Find the navigation bar CTA button element and replace its existing class/style with `class='btn' style='background-color:#FF5A36; color:#FFFFFF; border-radius:4px; padding:10px 20px; font-weight:700; font-size:14px; border:none;'` to match the standardised primary CTA style.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · Key Themes cards, mobile (390px)
findings.issue: The four theme cards appear to stack but each card's overlay text (session title and description) is very small and partially cut off at the card bottom edge, suggesting the card has a fixed pixel height that is too short for wrapped text on narrow screens.
findings.recommendation: Remove fixed height on theme cards for mobile and use min-height: 280px with the card expanding to fit content, ensuring overlay text is always fully visible.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a media query: `@media (max-width: 576px) { .theme-card { height: auto !important; min-height: 280px; } .theme-card .overlay-text { position: relative; background: rgba(10,37,64,0.85); padding: 12px; } }` — adjust selectors to match actual theme card class names.

findings.issue: On mobile the four stat blocks appear to render 2×2 but the text within each block wraps tightly with minimal padding, making the numbers hard to read and the label text truncating on the second line.
findings.recommendation: On mobile, increase internal cell padding to 16px and ensure stat number font-size reduces gracefully (e.g. 28px on mobile vs 40px desktop).
findings.fix_prompt: Add `@media (max-width: 576px) { .stats-item { padding: 16px 8px; text-align: center; } .stats-number { font-size: 28px; } .stats-label { font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.4; } }` — update selectors to match actual stat element class names.

findings.issue: On mobile the hero retains the dark background with the chess imagery but the event name 'Corporate Counsel and Compliance Exchange USA' wraps to 5+ lines at a large size, pushing the date and CTA buttons partially below the fold on a 390px screen. The primary CTA is not above the fold.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the hero heading font-size on mobile to 24–28px and tighten line-height so the event name, date, location, and CTA all fit within the first screen height.
findings.fix_prompt: Add: `@media (max-width: 576px) { .hero-event-title { font-size: 26px !important; line-height: 1.2; } .hero-section { padding-top: 24px; padding-bottom: 24px; } }` so the hero content compresses to keep the CTA button visible without scrolling on a 390px viewport.

findings.issue: The mobile navigation appears to compress the logo and nav items into the same row, making the logo very small (potentially below the brand minimum clear-space requirement) without a clear hamburger menu visible in the screenshot.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the mobile nav uses a hamburger/drawer pattern with the logo at full min-clear-space and the nav collapsed into a drawer.
findings.fix_prompt: In the mobile nav styles, add `@media (max-width: 768px) { .portal-navigation .logo img { height: 40px; width: auto; } .nav-items-container { display: none; } .hamburger-menu { display: block; } }` and ensure the hamburger toggle is wired to show/hide the nav drawer.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Primary CTA buttons site-wide (confirmed by axe-core: .aos-animate.btn-primary)
findings.issue: Primary call-to-action buttons (blue #0081ff background with white text) fail WCAG 2 AA contrast ratio — the contrast of white on #0081ff is approximately 3.0:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. This affects the most important interactive element on the page.
findings.recommendation: Change button background to a darker blue (#0053c2 or the brand primary #0A2540) which passes AA contrast with white text, or change to the brand accent #FF5A36 (contrast with white ≈ 3.7:1 — also marginal; prefer #0A2540 which exceeds 4.5:1).
findings.fix_prompt: In the dynamic stylesheet :root, set `--primary-color: #0A2540;` and `--primary-color-hover: #061829;`. This ensures all .btn-primary elements inherit a background colour that achieves approximately 16:1 contrast with white text, passing WCAG AA and AAA.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Hero section — event name and subtitle over background image, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: The hero background image shows chess pieces and people. In areas where the image is lighter (right side), the white event title text may have insufficient contrast. No full-width scrim overlay is visible in the screenshot — the image gradient appears partial.
findings.recommendation: Add a full-coverage dark scrim (e.g. linear-gradient from rgba(10,37,64,0.75) to rgba(10,37,64,0.55)) over the entire hero image to guarantee text contrast across all viewport widths.
findings.fix_prompt: On the hero section's background image container, add a pseudo-element or overlay div: `.hero-section::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(10,37,64,0.80) 0%, rgba(10,37,64,0.50) 100%); z-index: 1; }` and ensure all hero text elements have `position: relative; z-index: 2;`.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Theme cards — white text over image overlays, mobile
findings.issue: On mobile the theme card images are smaller and the gradient overlay compresses, making white text labels on some cards (particularly the lighter-background 'The Rookies' card) appear with insufficient contrast against the underlying image.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the card overlay gradient provides at least rgba(0,0,0,0.65) coverage behind all text, or add a solid text-shadow to all card headings as a fallback.
findings.fix_prompt: Add CSS: `.theme-card .card-text-overlay { background: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(10,37,64,0.85) 0%, rgba(10,37,64,0.4) 70%, transparent 100%); } .theme-card h3, .theme-card p { text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.8); }` — update selectors to match actual card class names.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Yellow (#ffd230) links and buttons throughout page
findings.issue: Links styled in the --link-color (#ffd230 yellow) appear on white backgrounds throughout the page (e.g. in the speakers section, navigation links). Yellow on white has a contrast ratio of approximately 1.6:1, which critically fails WCAG AA for both normal and large text.
findings.recommendation: Change --link-color to a dark value that passes contrast on white, such as #0A2540 (brand primary) or #0053c2, reserving yellow only for use on dark backgrounds.
findings.fix_prompt: In the dynamic stylesheet :root, change `--link-color: #0A2540;` and `--link-hover-color: #FF5A36;`. This ensures all `a:not(.btn)` links on white backgrounds have sufficient contrast while maintaining brand colour usage.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Photo Gallery section, desktop
findings.issue: Gallery images (confirmed by axe-core image-alt finding) include at least one image missing descriptive alt text, meaning screen reader users receive no information about gallery content.
findings.recommendation: Add descriptive alt attributes to all gallery images (e.g. alt='Attendees networking at Corporate Counsel Exchange 2025').
findings.fix_prompt: In the photo gallery HTML, find all `` elements within the gallery container that have empty or missing alt attributes and add descriptive alt text: e.g. ``. Use unique descriptions for each image.

findings.location: CTAs site-wide (hero, speakers, themes, sponsorship, footer)

findings.location: Theme cards (Key Themes section) vs Speaker cards, desktop
